scope: Native erlang:is_list/1 and complete X/Y list guard cases. This is the native nil-or-cons predicate, not proper-list validation.
adaptations: Return true for NIL or a cons, including improper lists, without traversing the tail. Charge one bounded native step in the BIF; no allocation, collection or new failure result is introduced.
Project both complete native is_list X/Y cases. Positive BIF admission is now an explicit per-arity ID whitelist with the same prior entries plus is_list/1, not a blanket BIF-kind permission.

Literal lowering overwrites x1023 on both branches, as for integer guards. Preserve those scratch facts, but never infer nonempty-cons access merely from a successful is_list test. Normalized verifier tests cover both scratch branches and refusal of get_hd without an independent nonempty-list proof.

Parameterize the existing predicate harness rather than copying it. Independently checked compiler/assembly fixtures cover NIL, proper/improper lists, non-list term classes, body/X/Y/literal guards and returned list survival across forced GC in the following allocation instruction. Only the integer mode claims the fused integer/allocation opcode.

Tests retain the mandatory VM reserve, exercise every GC allocation prefix, callback OOM versus accounted denial, allocation-free predicates and false guards, and every work prefix for true, false and NIL inputs with/without forced collection. Shared-worker tests cover exact bytes, exact/one-below budgets, reuse, peers and reclamation.
